summary: Fremont NF lookout in Lake County, Oregon: a D-6 cupola cabin built in 1923, replaced by a hip-roof house in 1954, and gone in 1972.

facts.design: D-6 cupola cabin (1923), a 12-by-12 house with a cupola; replaced in 1954 by a 14-by-14 hip-roof house
facts.status_note: The register says the D-6 cupola cabin was removed in 1972; Rex's page says the house burned, and firelookout.com says it was destroyed in 1972

staffing.status: staffed in the fire season: Mr. and Mrs. Jack Glasson at the station in 1924, Joe Frizzell on duty in 1938; in 1969 listed for emergency detection; no staffing end date in these sources

events.note: Rex's page quotes August and October 1923 items on the new house, which was completed and painted by October; the register and firelookout.com both give 1923 as the build year
Mr. and Mrs. Jack Glasson had been at the station continuously since April 16, per a Lake County Examiner item quoted on Rex's page
Joe Frizzell was the lookout on duty in September 1938
Visitors had a first-class view of the Black Cap fire from the lookout, per a Lake County Examiner item quoted on Rex's page
A 14-by-14 hip-roof lookout house replaced the old cupola house; total cost $4,171.93, with no catwalk
The 1969 lookout inventory shows the lookout used for emergency detection
The register says removed, firelookout.com says destroyed, and Rex's page says it burned

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources agree the house was gone by 1972 but describe its end three ways: the register says removed, firelookout.com says destroyed, and Rex's page says it burned. The story reports all three and does not choose one.

The register and firelookout.com tie the 1972 loss to the 1923 D-6 cupola cabin, but Rex's page says a 14x14 hip-roof house replaced the old cupola house in 1954 and says a house burned in 1972 without saying which one. The story says only 'the house' and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Brief record is accurate (gone, ground, Lake County, 2414 m). Build year 1923 is consistent across all three sources. The 1972 end is the only real disagreement (removed, destroyed, burned). Rex's page quotes its 1923 and 1924 items from newspapers and a forest history without giving the original citations. Search results for 'Cougar Peak lookout' also return a Montana lookout (Lolo NF) and a Wikidata entry for it; those are a different structure and were not used. Rex's page also says 'Cougar Peak' had a 1915 watch-tower plan; not used, because no source ties it to the 1923 house.
